sanskrit: sa evaṃ bruvatīṃ sītāṃ dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ nivartanārthe dharmātmā vākyam etad uvāca ha
english: As Sītā spoke thus, that knower of dharma, devoted to righteousness, that righteous soul, spoke these words to turn her back.

sanskrit: sīte mahākulīnāsi dharme ca niratā sadā ihācara svadharmaṃ tvaṃ mā yathā manasaḥ sukham
english: "Sītā, you are born of a great lineage and are ever devoted to dharma. Practise your own duty here — do not act merely as your heart desires."

sanskrit: sīte yathā tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tathā kāryaṃ tvayābale vane doṣā hi bahavo vadatas tān nibodha me
english: "Sītā, you must act as I shall tell you, O gentle one. The forest holds many hardships; hear me speak of them."

sanskrit: sīte vimucyatām eṣā vanavāsakṛtā matiḥ bahudoṣaṃ hi kāntāraṃ vanam ity abhidhīyate
english: "Sītā, abandon this resolve to dwell in the forest. What is called the wilderness is full of many dangers."

sanskrit: hitabuddhyā khalu vaco mayaitad abhidhīyate sadā sukhaṃ na jānāmi duḥkham eva sadā vanam
english: "I say this out of concern for your welfare: the forest knows no happiness — it is nothing but misery at every turn."

sanskrit: girinirjharasaṃbhūtā girikandaravāsinām siṃhānāṃ ninadā duḥkhāḥ śrotuṃ duḥkham ato vanam
english: "The roars of lions dwelling in mountain caves, rising from mountain torrents — these are dreadful to hear. For this reason, the forest is suffering."

sanskrit: supyate parṇaśayyāsu svayaṃ bhagnāsu bhūtale rātriṣu śramakhinnena tasmād duḥkhataraṃ vanam
english: "One must sleep on leaf-beds, broken and spread on the bare ground, weary from exertion through the nights. For this reason, the forest is yet harder to bear."

sanskrit: upavāsaś ca kartavyā yathāprāṇena maithili jaṭābhāraś ca kartavyo valkalāmbaradhāriṇā
english: "Fasts must be kept, O Maithilī, as one's strength allows; matted locks must be worn, and garments of bark must be borne."

sanskrit: atīva vātas timiraṃ bubhukṣā cātra nityaśaḥ bhayāni ca mahānty atra tato duḥkhataraṃ vanam
english: "There the wind is fierce, the darkness deep, and hunger constant; great terrors abound — for this reason, the forest is harder still."

sanskrit: sarīsṛpāś ca bahavo bahurūpāś ca bhāmini caranti pṛthivīṃ darpād ato dukhataraṃ vanam
english: "Many reptiles of many forms, O passionate one, crawl boldly over the ground. For this reason, the forest is very hard to endure."

sanskrit: nadīnilayanāḥ sarpā nadīkuṭilagāminaḥ tiṣṭhanty āvṛtya panthānam ato duḥkhataraṃ vanam
english: "Serpents that dwell in rivers, winding through their bends, lie coiled across the paths. For this reason, the forest is harder to bear."

sanskrit: pataṃgā vṛścikāḥ kīṭā daṃśāś ca maśakaiḥ saha bādhante nityam abale sarvaṃ duḥkham ato vanam
english: "Locusts, scorpions, worms, horse-flies and mosquitoes together torment one ceaselessly, O gentle one. All of it is suffering — therefore the forest is misery."

sanskrit: drumāḥ kaṇṭakinaś caiva kuśakāśāś ca bhāmini vane vyākulaśākhāgrās tena duḥkhataraṃ vanam
english: "Thorny trees, and kusa grass and kāśa reeds, with their branch-tips tangled in the forest, O passionate one — for this reason the forest is harder to endure."

sanskrit: tad alaṃ te vanaṃ gatvā kṣamaṃ na hi vanaṃ tava vimṛśann iha paśyāmi bahudoṣataraṃ vanam
english: "Therefore, enough of going to the forest. The forest is not fit for you. Considering it carefully, I see the forest as full of many faults indeed."

sanskrit: vanaṃ tu netuṃ na kṛtā matis tadā babhūva rāmeṇa yadā mahātmanā na tasya sītā vacanaṃ cakāra tat tato 'bravīd rāmam idaṃ suduḥkhitā
english: But even after the great-souled Rāma resolved not to take her to the forest, Sītā paid no heed to his words. Then, deeply distressed, she spoke to Rāma thus.

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sītā rāmasya duḥkhitā prasaktāśrumukhī mandam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing Rāma's words, Sītā, stricken with grief, her face streaming with tears, spoke these words slowly.

sanskrit: ye tvayā kīrtitā doṣā vane vastavyatāṃ prati guṇān ity eva tān viddhi tava snehapuraskṛtān
english: "The hardships you have named regarding life in the forest — know that I regard all of them as virtues, offered forth by your love for me."

sanskrit: tvayā ca saha gantavyaṃ mayā gurujanājñayā tvadviyogena me rāma tyaktavyam iha jīvitam
english: "I must go with you — such is the command of my elders. Without you, Rāma, I must give up this life here."

sanskrit: na ca māṃ tvatsamīpastham api śaknoti rāghava surāṇām īśvaraḥ śakraḥ pradharṣayitum ojasā
english: "Standing at your side, O Rāghava, not even Śakra, lord of the gods, could overpower me by his might."

sanskrit: patihīnā tu yā nārī na sā śakṣyati jīvitum kāmam evaṃvidhaṃ rāma tvayā mama vidarśitam
english: "A woman bereft of her husband cannot live — such is the very truth, Rāma, that you have yourself shown me."

sanskrit: atha cāpi mahāprājña brāhmaṇānāṃ mayā śrutam purā pitṛgṛhe satyaṃ vastavyaṃ kila me vane
english: "And besides, O greatly wise one, I once heard from brāhmaṇas, truly, in my father's house, that I am destined to dwell in the forest."

sanskrit: lakṣaṇibhyo dvijātibhyaḥ śrutvāhaṃ vacanaṃ gṛhe vanavāsakṛtotsāhā nityam eva mahābala
english: "Hearing the words of those auspicious twice-born sages at home, O mighty one, I have ever since felt a keenness for living in the forest."

sanskrit: ādeśo vanavāsasya prāptavyaḥ sa mayā kila sā tvayā saha tatrāhaṃ yāsyāmi priya nānyathā
english: "That sojourn in the forest, so foretold, must come to me — and there, beloved, I shall go with you alone, no other way."

sanskrit: kṛtādeśā bhaviṣyāmi gamiṣyāmi saha tvayā kālaś cāyaṃ samutpannaḥ satyavāg bhavatu dvijaḥ
english: "The prophecy shall be fulfilled — I shall go with you. Now the time has come; let the brāhmaṇa's word prove true."

sanskrit: vanavāse hi jānāmi duḥkhāni bahudhā kila prāpyante niyataṃ vīra puruṣair akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: "I know well that in forest-life, many kinds of suffering are surely encountered by men of undisciplined spirit, O hero."

sanskrit: kanyayā ca pitur gehe vanavāsaḥ śruto mayā bhikṣiṇyāḥ sādhuvṛttāyā mama mātur ihāgrataḥ
english: "And as a girl in my father's house, I heard of forest-dwelling from a wandering ascetic woman of virtuous conduct, here in the presence of my mother."

sanskrit: prasāditaś ca vai pūrvaṃ tvaṃ vai bahuvidhaṃ prabho gamanaṃ vanavāsasya kāṅkṣitaṃ hi saha tvayā
english: "You have been entreated in many ways before, O lord — for the journey of forest-dwelling together with you is what I have longed for."

sanskrit: kṛtakṣaṇāhaṃ bhadraṃ te gamanaṃ prati rāghava vanavāsasya śūrasya caryā hi mama rocate
english: "I am ready and resolved for the journey, O Rāghava — bless you! The wandering life of the forest, proper to a hero, is pleasing to me."

sanskrit: śuddhātman premabhāvād dhi bhaviṣyāmi vikalmaṣā bhartāram anugacchantī bhartā hi mama daivatam
english: "O pure-souled one, following my husband out of love, I shall be free of all sin — for a husband is my very deity."

sanskrit: pretyabhāve 'pi kalyāṇaḥ saṃgamo me saha tvayā śrutir hi śrūyate puṇyā brāhmaṇānāṃ yaśasvinām
english: "Even in the life after death, union with you is auspicious for me — so runs the holy scripture that is heard from the illustrious brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: iha loke ca pitṛbhir yā strī yasya mahāmate adbhir dattā svadharmeṇa pretyabhāve 'pi tasya sā
english: "O greatly wise one, a woman who has been given by her parents to a man here in this world with the rite of water and in accord with dharma — she belongs to him even in the afterlife."

sanskrit: evam asmāt svakāṃ nārīṃ suvṛttāṃ hi pativratām nābhirocayase netuṃ tvaṃ māṃ keneha hetunā
english: "Given all this, for what reason do you not wish to take me — your own wife, of good conduct and devoted to her husband?"

sanskrit: bhaktāṃ pativratāṃ dīnāṃ māṃ samāṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ netum arhasi kākutstha samānasukhaduḥkhinīm
english: "You ought to take me, O Kākutstha — devoted, faithful to my vow, helpless, equal in joy and in sorrow — one who shares equally in happiness and grief."

sanskrit: yadi māṃ duḥkhitām evaṃ vanaṃ netuṃ na cecchasi viṣam agniṃ jalaṃ vāham āsthāsye mṛtyukāraṇāt
english: "If you do not wish to take me, thus wretched, to the forest, then I shall resort to poison, fire, or water as the cause of my death."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ taṃ sā yācate gamanaṃ prati nānumene mahābāhus tāṃ netuṃ vijanaṃ vanam
english: Even as she pleaded with him in many ways for permission to go, the mighty-armed Rāma did not consent to taking her into the desolate forest.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā cintāṃ maithilī samupāgatā snāpayantīva gām uṣṇair aśrubhir nayanacyutaiḥ
english: Spoken to in this way, Maithilī fell into deep anguish, and the hot tears flowing from her eyes seemed to drench the earth.

sanskrit: cintayantīṃ tathā tāṃ tu nivartayitum ātmavān krodhāviṣṭāṃ tu vaidehīṃ kākutstho bahv asāntvayat
english: As she brooded thus, the self-composed Kākutstha consoled Vaidehī at length, even as she was overcome with anger, trying to turn her away from her resolve.

sanskrit: sāntvyamānā tu rāmeṇa maithilī janakātmajā vanavāsanimittāya bhartāram idam abravīt
english: But even while being consoled by Rāma, Maithilī, daughter of Janaka, spoke these words to her husband in order to go to the forest.

sanskrit: sā tam uttamasaṃvignā sītā vipulavakṣasaṃ praṇayāc cābhimānāc ca paricikṣepa rāghavam
english: Deeply agitated, Sītā embraced broad-chested Rāghava out of both affection and wounded pride.

sanskrit: kiṃ tvāmanyata vaidehaḥ pitā me mithilādhipaḥ rāma jāmātaraṃ prāpya striyaṃ puruṣavigraham
english: "What must my father, Vaideha, lord of Mithilā, have thought of you, Rāma — a son-in-law who has a woman's form in the shape of a man?"

sanskrit: anṛtaṃ balaloko 'yam ajñānād yad dhi vakṣyati tejo nāsti paraṃ rāme tapatīva divākare
english: "False and ignorant is what the world will say — that there is no supreme valour in Rāma — when he blazes like the sun in the sky."

sanskrit: kiṃ hi kṛtvā viṣaṇṇas tvaṃ kuto vā bhayam asti te yat parityaktukāmas tvaṃ mām ananyaparāyaṇām
english: "What have you done to make you downcast? Or whence comes the fear that makes you wish to abandon me who have no refuge but you?"

sanskrit: dyumatsenasutaṃ vīra satyavantam anuvratām sāvitrīm iva māṃ viddhi tvam ātmavaśavartinīm
english: "Know me, O hero, to be like Sāvitrī who was devoted to Satyavat, son of Dyumatsena — wholly devoted to you, under your authority alone."

sanskrit: na tv ahaṃ manasāpy anyaṃ draṣṭāsmi tvadṛte 'nagha tvayā rāghava gaccheyaṃ yathānyā kulapāṃsanī
english: "I have never looked upon another man, even in my mind, O sinless one. How could I go without you, O Rāghava, like a woman who dishonours her family?"

sanskrit: svayaṃ tu bhāryāṃ kaumārīṃ ciram adhyuṣitāṃ satīm śailūṣa iva māṃ rāma parebhyo dātum icchasi
english: "And yet, Rāma, you yourself wish to hand me over to others — your wife, taken in youth, long cohabited with, chaste — as a stage-dancer might his own."

sanskrit: sa mām anādāya vanaṃ na tvaṃ prasthātum arhasi tapo vā yadi vāraṇyaṃ svargo vā syāt saha tvayā
english: "Without taking me, you should not set out for the forest. Whether it be penance, wilderness, or heaven — all is to be with you."

sanskrit: na ca me bhavitā tatra kaś cit pathi pariśramaḥ pṛṣṭhatas tava gacchantyā vihāraśayaneṣv api
english: "There will not be any hardship for me on the path, following behind you, whether in the places of wandering or in sleeping."

sanskrit: kuśakāśaśareṣīkā ye ca kaṇṭakino drumāḥ tūlājinasamasparśā mārge mama saha tvayā
english: "The kuśa grass, kāśa reeds, śara rushes, and thorny trees along the way — to me, travelling with you, their touch will be as soft as cotton or hide."

sanskrit: mahāvāta samuddhūtaṃ yan mām avakariṣyati rajo ramaṇa tan manye parārdhyam iva candanam
english: "The dust that a great wind will scatter upon me, O beloved, I shall regard as the most precious sandalwood paste."

sanskrit: śādvaleṣu yad āsiṣye vanānte vanagoracā kuthāstaraṇatalpeṣu kiṃ syāt sukhataraṃ tataḥ
english: "Resting on the grassy meadows at the forest's edge, familiar with the forest, on beds spread with kuthā grass — what could be more pleasant than that?"

sanskrit: patraṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ yat tvam alpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu dāsyasi svayam āhṛtya tan me 'mṛtarasopamam
english: "Whatever leaf, root, or fruit you yourself gather and give me — whether little or much — that will be like the taste of nectar to me."

sanskrit: na mātur na pitus tatra smariṣyāmi na veśmanaḥ ārtavāny upabhuñjānā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
english: "There I shall not think of my mother, nor my father, nor the house, as I enjoy the seasonal flowers and fruits."

sanskrit: na ca tatra gataḥ kiṃ cid draṣṭum arhasi vipriyam matkṛte na ca te śoko na bhaviṣyāmi durbharā
english: "There you shall not see anything unpleasant on my account; there will be no sorrow for you because of me, nor shall I be a burden to you."

sanskrit: yas tvayā saha sa svargo nirayo yas tvayā vinā iti jānan parāṃ prītiṃ gaccha rāma mayā saha
english: "Where you are is heaven; where you are not is hell — knowing this supreme love of mine, go, Rāma, with me."

sanskrit: atha mām evam avyagrāṃ vanaṃ naiva nayiṣyasi viṣam adyaiva pāsyāmi mā viśaṃ dviṣatāṃ vaśam
english: "But if you will not take me — thus calm and resolved — to the forest, I shall this very day drink poison. I will not fall under the power of your enemies."

sanskrit: paścād api hi duḥkhena mama naivāsti jīvitam ujjhitāyās tvayā nātha tadaiva maraṇaṃ varam
english: "Even thereafter, life abandoned by you in sorrow is no life at all, O lord — death at that very moment is better."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi sahituṃ śokaṃ muhūrtam api notsahe kiṃ punar daśavarṣāṇi trīṇi caikaṃ ca duḥkhitā
english: "This grief I cannot bear even for a moment — how much less, wretched, for thirteen years?"

sanskrit: iti sā śokasaṃtaptā vilapya karuṇaṃ bahu cukrośa patim āyastā bhṛśam āliṅgya sasvaram
english: Thus she, scorched by grief, having lamented piteously and at length, clung tightly to her husband, weeping aloud in her anguish.

sanskrit: sā viddhā bahubhir vākyair digdhair iva gajāṅganā cira saṃniyataṃ bāṣpaṃ mumocāgnim ivāraṇiḥ
english: Pierced by many sharp words as a she-elephant by poisoned arrows, she released the tears long suppressed, like fire released from the araṇi wood.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ sphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ vāri saṃtāpasaṃbhavam netrābhyāṃ parisusrāva paṅkajābhyām ivodakam
english: Water clear as crystal, born of her anguish, flowed from her two eyes as water flows from two lotuses.

sanskrit: tāṃ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ visaṃjñām iva duḥkhitām uvāca vacanaṃ rāmaḥ pariviśvāsayaṃs tadā
english: Embracing her in his arms — she who was grief-stricken and as if unconscious — Rāma then spoke words of reassurance.

sanskrit: na devi tava duḥkhena svargam apy abhirocaye na hi me 'sti bhayaṃ kiṃ cit svayambhor iva sarvataḥ
english: "O goddess, I do not desire even heaven purchased by your suffering. I have no fear from any quarter, like Svayambhū himself."

sanskrit: tava sarvam abhiprāyam avijñāya śubhānane vāsaṃ na rocaye 'raṇye śaktimān api rakṣaṇe
english: "Without knowing your full mind, O fair-faced one, I did not wish to dwell in the forest — even though I am capable of protecting you."

sanskrit: yat sṛṣṭāsi mayā sārdhaṃ vanavāsāya maithili na vihātuṃ mayā śakyā kīrtir ātmavatā yathā
english: "Since you were created to share forest-dwelling with me, O Maithilī, you cannot be forsaken by me — as a self-respecting man cannot forsake his honour."

sanskrit: dharmas tu gajanāsoru sadbhir ācaritaḥ purā taṃ cāham anuvarte 'dya yathā sūryaṃ suvarcalā
english: "The dharma practised of old by the good — that I follow today, O elephant-gaited one, as Suvarcalā follows the sun."

sanskrit: eṣa dharmas tu suśroṇi pitur mātuś ca vaśyatā ataś cājñāṃ vyatikramya nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe
english: "This is dharma, O fair-hipped one — to be subject to one's father and mother. Having transgressed their command, I cannot bear to live."

sanskrit: sa māṃ pitā yathā śāsti satyadharmapathe sthitaḥ tathā vartitum icchāmi sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ anugacchasva māṃ bhīru sahadharmacarī bhava
english: "I wish to conduct myself as my father instructs me, he who stands firm on the path of truth and righteousness — for that is eternal dharma. Follow me, O timid one; be my companion in dharma."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyaś ca ratnāni bhikṣukebhyaś ca bhojanam dehi cāśaṃsamānebhyaḥ saṃtvarasva ca māciram
english: "Give jewels to the brāhmaṇas and food to the mendicants; give to those who seek — and make haste, do not delay."

sanskrit: anukūlaṃ tu sā bhartur jñātvā gamanam ātmanaḥ kṣipraṃ pramuditā devī dātum evopacakrame
english: Learning that her husband's departure and her own journey were now agreed, the goddess Sītā, joyful, swiftly set about giving gifts.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭā paripūrṇamānasā yaśasvinī bhartur avekṣya bhāṣitam dhanāni ratnāni ca dātum aṅganā pracakrame dharmabhṛtāṃ manasvinī
english: Then she, elated and with heart full of joy, the illustrious and noble-minded woman, heeding her husband's words, set about giving wealth and jewels to those who uphold dharma.
